Operator overloading, custom exceptions and extension methods

Try one operator, one custom error type and one extension method before combining them.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A console playground for C# features

Run small experiments with objects, reusable helpers, lists and work that takes time. Each experiment prints results in the console.

These experiments use temporary values rather than a student database.

Check the result

Run the console app, find the part for this lesson and compare its printed result with the explanation.

An operator overload teaches a type what a symbol means. An exception says a job could not be completed. An extension method adds a convenient method-call spelling without changing the original type.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Three tools, three jobs

public readonly record struct Money(decimal Amount)
{
    public static Money operator +(Money a, Money b) => new(a.Amount + b.Amount);
}
public class EnrollmentException(string message) : Exception(message);
public static class StudentExtensions
{
    public static string Greeting(this string name) => $"Hello, {name}";
}

Money(10) + Money(5) returns a new Money with Amount 15. The compiler chooses this overload because both operands are Money. Operators should behave predictably. Use exceptions for exceptional failures; use TryParse or validation for ordinary invalid input. Extension methods must be static and declare this on the first parameter; they cannot access another class’s private data.

Expected output and debugging

Money total: 15
Age cannot be negative.
Hello, lefa

The full lab catches EnrollmentException so later examples still run. Catch the most specific useful exception, and use throw; when rethrowing to keep the original stack trace. Never silently swallow an exception.

Try it yourself

Add subtraction for Money.

Worked answer

public static Money operator -(Money a, Money b) => new(a.Amount - b.Amount); Add it inside Money.

When should an extension method be avoided?

Worked answer

Avoid hiding important business rules in surprising extensions. A normal service or instance method can make ownership clearer.

Predict and practise

Does an extension method change the source code of string?

Check your prediction

No. It is a static helper called with instance-like syntax.

Make one change

Call the supplied extension helper with a different input.

Worked guidance

Find the static method with this on its first parameter. Change the value passed by the caller.

Try independently

Create your own extension helper and explain which type it works on.
